findings: Comparison target is judge measurement, not a permission matrix: whether a creative-writing judge can separate refusal from suitability, and both from schema or quote failure, on ordinary-for-fiction adult sex, violence, profanity, and non-explicit controls.

Two arms only. Holistic: one broad prompt that jointly scores fulfillment, form, and ordinary-fiction suitability. HBQ: independent binary questions, each asked in isolation with no other criteria in context, no shared rationale, and no cross-item memory.

Minimal slices, reuse existing labels only, no new human judges. Four content families (explicit adult sex as narrative fiction, graphic violence as narrative fiction, heavy profanity, non-explicit controls). Within each family, a compact completion mix: full write, hard refuse, soft or partial refuse, schema-invalid, quote or excerpt failure, and on-topic write that existing labels already mark unsuitable. Cap at the smallest N that still fills every cell from current gold; do not expand with new annotation.

Outcome measures are cell-level, not a taxonomy. Primary: refusal precision/recall vs existing refuse labels; confusion among refuse vs schema-fail vs quote-fail vs completed write. Secondary: suitability agreement only against existing suitable/unsuitable labels for that slice. Contrast metrics: holistic vs HBQ disagreement rate, control over-flag rate on non-explicit items, and criterion leakage (a sex-item answer shifting violence or profanity answers). Report calibration of binary HBQ yes-rate vs holistic joint score.

Bounded question-level retry: retry only unparseable judge output, max one retry per question, with the same frozen prompt. Never retry to change a content decision. Holistic retries the single call; HBQ retries only the failed question. Seed, temperature, and stop conditions fixed. Fail-closed to schema-fail if the retry is still unparseable.

Defensible claims stay inside this compact set: judges can or cannot tell refusal from form failure; holistic and HBQ do or do not differ on control over-flag and criterion independence. Do not claim that any class of sexual, violent, or profane fiction is permitted, disallowed, safe, or product-policy-compliant.
recommendations: Freeze a tiny reuse-only pack: 4 families × 6 completion types, 3–5 existing labeled items per cell if available, else drop the empty cell and disclose it. Keep prompts, model, and decoding identical across arms.

HBQ items must be four independent binaries only: (1) refuses the writing request, (2) violates required schema, (3) fails the requested quote or excerpt constraint, (4) is ordinary fictional treatment per existing suitability labels. Ask one question per call. Ban compound wording such as allowed, disallowed, harmful, or policy-compliant.
Holistic prompt may request the same four fields in one JSON object, but must not add extra moral, legal, or permission axes. Score field-wise against the same gold as HBQ.

Analyze with a 4-way confusion table plus control false-positive rate. Pre-register that suitability is not permission, and that a high suitability score on explicit fiction is not a product go-ahead.

Claims language: allowed — “On this labeled set, judge arm A confused refusal with quote failure at rate X; arm B at rate Y.” Forbidden — “The product allows explicit sex / graphic violence / profanity.” If cells are sparse, claim only directional contrast, not coverage or human parity.
risks: Holistic judges will collapse refuse, schema-fail, and “I would not write this” into one negative, inflating refusal and hiding form bugs.
HBQ independence can still leak if question text names the content family, producing a de facto permission taxonomy.
Existing labels may encode rater policy, not ordinary-fiction norms, especially on sex and violence; reusing them without new judges can launder that policy as measurement.
One parse retry can silently select the more conservative judge sample if the first decode was a valid write-suitable judgment.
Overclaim risk is high: compact fiction slices are not safety certification, not child-safety tests, and not evidence of what the product should generate.
output.summary: Run a reuse-only, no-new-judges contrast of one holistic creative-writing judge versus independent binary HBQ questions on four compact slices: ordinary-for-fiction explicit adult sex, violence, profanity, and non-explicit controls. Score refusal, schema failure, quote failure, and existing-label suitability as separate outcomes; retry at most once per question and only on unparseable judge output. Use the results to compare judge error modes, not to mint a content-permission taxonomy or product-allowance claim.
